arm: Full multi-agent loop (Planner, Research, Skeptic, Writer, Evaluator; up to two rounds)
selection: the first 10 set-1a questions with a named U.S. product, in file order, fixed before any run

answers.finding: No U.S. prescribing information for afatinib mentioning eyelash growth, hypertrichosis, or related terms found in sources.

US label v82 (effective 2026-10-14) mentions renal failure/impairment as reason for dose modification (sections 2.4, 2.5, 8.6) but does not mention tumour lysis syndrome in Boxed Warning, Warnings and Precautions, Contraindications, or Adverse Reactions
US label v21 (2026-03-02) lists immune-mediated colitis in postmarketing experience (6.2), a specific subtype of colitis, but not in boxed warning, warnings/precautions, or contraindications.
U.S. label v36 (effective 2026-02-09) includes hyperammonemic encephalopathy in Warnings and Precautions 5.1 Hepatotoxicity with management guidance.
U.S. label (Zoloft v7) lists rhabdomyolysis in post-marketing experience but does not mention multiple acyl-coenzyme A dehydrogenase deficiency (MADD).
U.S. label (Bactrim v18, effective 2024-12-30) includes circulatory shock in WARNINGS (Hypersensitivity and Other Serious or Fatal Reactions) and ADVERSE REACTIONS sections.

Yescarta US label v23 (effective 2026-08-06) does not contain the specific terms 'immune-mediated enterocolitis' or 'immune effector cell-associated enteritis'; only mentions diarrhea as a common adverse reaction in section 6 and MedGuide.
No US label sections (Boxed Warning, Warnings and Precautions, Contraindications, Adverse Reactions, postmarketing) mention pyoderma gangrenosum for brodalumab.
US label v24 (effective 2026-07-28) includes warning in Warnings and Precautions 5.8 and Drug Interactions 7.3 about digoxin immunoassay interference.
US label v18 (2025-03-05) lists hallucinations as symptom of serotonin syndrome (5.2) and in severe hyponatremia (5.7), not as independent adverse reaction.
